title: Exterior Painting in Ocala, FL | Stucco, Siding & Trim
description: Exterior painting in Ocala, FL built for intense sun and summer storms. Elastomeric on stucco, 100% acrylic on siding, and up to a 10-year written warranty.
h1: Exterior Painting in Ocala, FL That Stands Up to Sun and Storms
heroIntro: An Ocala house bakes on its south and west faces and stays damp through a long, stormy summer. Each side of yours gets the prep and coating its own exposure calls for.

sections.h2: Read the elevations before you pick the paint
body: On most Ocala houses, the south and west walls tell the real story. Those elevations take the afternoon sun, so pigment chalks and fades there long before the shaded north side shows wear. Meanwhile, the lower foot of siding and stucco catches rain splash and sprinkler overspray, and that constant dampness invites algae and soft wood. Good exterior painting in Ocala, FL starts with photographing every elevation and pricing the repairs each one actually needs. Our article on sun damage and paint restoration in Ocala shows what to look for.

sections.h2: Ocala substrates and how we coat them
body: Out in Silver Springs Shores and Marion Oaks, a lot of houses are stucco, and fine cracks come with the territory. Those cracks are cleaned and filled, and then the walls get an elastomeric coating that gives with minor movement rather than cracking along with it. Bigger stucco problems go to our stucco repair and painting crew first.

Around Tuscawilla and Historic Downtown, the porch columns, wood siding, and trim on the older houses get scraped until the old paint stops lifting, soft boards get swapped for new lumber, and raw wood gets primer. Siding and trim then get premium 100% acrylic. Mid-century block homes get careful caulking along fascia and window joints, plus a breathable acrylic system on the masonry.
bullets: Every side of the house washed, with mildew treated
Rot, fascia, and trim replacement priced from walkthrough photos
Cracks, gaps, and popped nails sealed, and primer on any raw wood
Two complete finish coats, with any sprayed section rolled or brushed in afterward
Windows, light fixtures, landscaping, and the driveway covered before work begins

sections.h2: Timing an Ocala exterior around the summer storms
body: Our preferred exterior season runs October through May, when humidity drops and afternoon storms are rare. When an Ocala job has to happen in summer, the crew is on site at first light, checks the dew point, watches the radar, and packs up well before a storm could hit wet paint. The painting on a whole house normally runs three to seven working days, with washing and drying counted separately, and we usually start one to three weeks after you approve. For the broader picture, see how weather affects house painting in Florida.

sections.h2: Ocala exterior warranty and final sign-off
body: Our workmanship on Ocala exteriors is warrantied in writing for up to 10 years, and the paint itself carries its maker's warranty as well. Your estimate spells out which product line goes on the house. Before the crew leaves, the two of you walk every side with the punch list, and you sign once every item has been made right. Each color gets its own labelled can of leftover paint.
For the full picture, see our exterior painting service page, add Ocala pressure washing to the same visit, or head back to the Ocala location page.

faqs.q: Can you paint my Ocala home's exterior in summer?
faqs.a: Yes, with some adjustments. Summer crews in Ocala begin at dawn and keep an eye on the dew point and the storm radar all day. Still, the months from October to May make exterior work easiest.

faqs.q: Will you fix rotted trim on my Ocala house before painting?
faqs.a: Yes. Swapping rotten fascia and trim is built into prep. What the crew lead photographs on the walkthrough is priced on your written estimate, and nothing new is added later unless you approve it.

faqs.q: Will one coat be enough to refresh my Ocala exterior?
faqs.a: No. Every Ocala exterior gets at least two full coats, and a third goes on when the color changes a lot or the surface is porous, as weathered stucco often is.

faqs.q: Do you paint outbuildings on Ocala horse properties?
faqs.a: Yes. A barn, shed, or other outbuilding can go on the same estimate as the house, and we pick the right coating for each one's surfaces.
